Hi Mike / Sarah —

Thanks again for the demo this morning. Quick recap and the items we agreed to follow up on related to data handling and support access so your security team can proceed with qualification: 

1) PII classification & retention: you flagged two classes of PII from submitted documents (patient identifiers + free-text notes). We've attached the high-level mapping (redwood-privacy-highlevel.pdf). Please confirm the retention windows you need for each data class — you mentioned 7 years for patient records and 90 days for transient logs during the call.
2) Data residency: option to pin to us-east-1 or eu-west-1. You said primary production must remain in US but analytics can be EU. Confirm whether you require contractual residency for all backups.
3) Logging & audit trails: we capture token-level audit trails and operator actions; need to confirm log retention and access controls. I'll share a sample schema and retention table (mnsg-data-retention-table.xlsx).
4) Support access / RBAC & break-glass: proposed model is role-based with 3 tiers (read-only observers, support operators with scoped backfills, and emergency break-glass). You requested a clear timeline and runbook for break-glass with approver flows. Attached is a simple explainer diagram (support-breakglass-flow.png).

Next steps we committed to:
- Redwood: provide the short privacy mapping + sample retention table and the break-glass runbook draft (deliver by EOD Wed 8/25). (Owner: me)
- Magnus: confirm required retention windows per data class and any contractual residency restrictions (Owner: Mike; by 8/26).
- Aditya: review technical feasibility of limiting KV-cache persistence to region-only backups and confirm logging granularity (Owner: Aditya; by 8/25).

If that aligns, I'll package the artifacts and a one-page summary for your security and procurement teams.

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz

Vanessa —

Quick technical notes from the runtime side after reviewing the notes and attachments:

- PII handling: we can flag patient identifiers at ingestion and enforce tokenization or field redaction before model input. That will add ~5-10ms/req at the ingestion pipeline.
- Retention: we support per-tenant retention TTL for KV caches and logs. Backups are region-scoped; we can configure that to avoid cross-region replicas if required.
- Logs: we provide structured audit events (user, action, model, tokens affected, timestamp). We can produce a redacted token count instead of raw tokens for compliance.
- Break-glass: recommend a HSM/KMS rewrapped temporary ACL that is time-bound (15–30 min) and logged with multi-party approval. Need to confirm whether Magnus requires an OOB (phone) approver.

I'll draft a short technical appendix for the break-glass flow that maps to the runbook and include an example of the audit event format. Assigning to myself to have a draft up by 8/25.

- Aditya
Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com

Thanks Vanessa — this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Retention: patient records = 7 years (state-mandated), transcripts/free-text = 3 years, operational logs = 180 days. Backups must be stored in the US only; analytics exports to EU are allowed but must be pseudonymized first.
- Break-glass: we prefer a two-approver model for any emergency access window >10 minutes, with automated email + Slack alert. Phone-based OOB approval is possible but prefer a joined Slack channel for rapid verification.
- Audit evidence: security will want an example CSV of audit events for a week (not real PII). Can you provide a redacted sample?

We'll get you the formal retention table from our compliance folks by COB Thursday 8/26. Appreciate the ownership on the runbook.

-Mike
Director, Infrastructure Security | Magnus Health
